---
title: Spectral Integration on a Disk
---

This page describes [[numcosmo-math|NcmSpectralPolar]], which integrates functions on a
disk of radius $R$ in polar coordinates $(r, \theta)$, with $0 \le r \le R$ and $\theta$
in an interval of length $2\pi$, or on an annular sector of the disk, the region between
two radii and two angles. The integrand may have a power law in $r$ at the origin,
$r = 0$, and at the edge of the disk, $r = R$. One use is the marginalization of the galaxy
shape likelihood over the intrinsic ellipticity, where the population and the noise
factors have these power laws
([Shape Marginalization by Spectral Panels](../../nc/lss/galaxy/wl_shape_marginalization_spectral.qmd)).

The disk is divided into panels, rectangles in $(r, \theta)$. On each panel the integrand
is approximated by a Chebyshev polynomial in $r$ and $\theta$, and the polynomial is
integrated. On the panels that touch $r = 0$ or $r = R$, the power law of that end is left
out of the polynomial, and the polynomial is integrated against it. The degree is raised
on nested grids until the convergence test of [Spectral Methods](spectral.qmd) holds in
both variables; a panel whose degree reaches the limit is bisected. For an integrand with
one narrow maximum the edges of the panels are placed around it
([Edges for One Peak](#edges-for-one-peak)). The polynomials of the panels also
approximate the function itself
([Approximation on the Panels](#approximation-on-the-panels)).

## The Integral and its Panels

The function [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_polar_integrate]] computes
$$
I \equiv \int\!\!\int r^a (R - r)^b \, G (r, \theta) \, \mathrm{d}r \, \mathrm{d}\theta ,
\tag{1}
$$
where $R$ is the radius of the disk, $a > -1$ is the exponent of the power law at the
origin, $b > -1$ the exponent of the power law at the edge, and $G (r, \theta)$ is smooth
at $r = 0$ and at $r = R$. The domain of the integral is given by the edges of the panels,
defined below. The polar Jacobian $r$ is included in $r^a$: a density in the plane,
regular at the origin and integrated with
$\mathrm{d}^2 x = r \, \mathrm{d}r \, \mathrm{d}\theta$, has $a = 1$.

The radial edges $0 \le r_0 < r_1 < \dots < r_{n_r} \le R$ and the angular edges
$\theta_0 < \theta_1 < \dots < \theta_{n_\theta}$, with
$\theta_{n_\theta} - \theta_0 \le 2\pi$, split the domain into $n_r n_\theta$ panels. A
panel is the rectangle $[r_a, r_b] \times [\theta_a, \theta_b]$ between two consecutive
radial edges and two consecutive angular edges, with half widths
$$
h_r \equiv \frac{r_b - r_a}{2}, \qquad h_\theta \equiv \frac{\theta_b - \theta_a}{2} .
$$
The weight is not infinitely differentiable at $r = 0$ unless $a$ is a non-negative
integer, and at $r = R$ unless $b$ is one; for $-1 < a < 0$ or $-1 < b < 0$ it is
singular there, with a finite integral. Only the panels that touch $r = 0$ or $r = R$
contain these points. On a panel, the exponents left in the weight are
$$
c_a \equiv \begin{cases} a, & r_a = 0, \\ 0, & r_a > 0, \end{cases}
\qquad
c_b \equiv \begin{cases} b, & r_b = R, \\ 0, & r_b < R, \end{cases}
$$
and the rest of the weight, which is smooth on the panel, multiplies $G$:
$$
F (r, \theta) \equiv r^{a - c_a} (R - r)^{b - c_b} \, G (r, \theta) .
\tag{2}
$$
The function $F$ is expanded on the panel. The contribution of the panel to Eq. (1) is the
integral of $r^{c_a} (R - r)^{c_b} F$ over it.

## Expansion on a Panel

With the Chebyshev variables $s_r, s_\theta \in [-1, 1]$,
$$
r = \frac{r_a + r_b}{2} + h_r s_r, \qquad
\theta = \frac{\theta_a + \theta_b}{2} + h_\theta s_\theta ,
$$
the function $F$ is sampled on the tensor grid of Chebyshev--Lobatto nodes of levels $l_r$
and $l_\theta$,
$$
s_{r, i} = \cos \left( \frac{i \pi}{N_r} \right), \quad i = 0, \dots, N_r, \qquad
s_{\theta, j} = \cos \left( \frac{j \pi}{N_\theta} \right), \quad j = 0, \dots, N_\theta ,
$$
with $N_r \equiv 2^{l_r}$ and $N_\theta \equiv 2^{l_\theta}$. A type-I discrete cosine
transform in each direction gives the coefficients $c^{kl}$ of
$$
F (r, \theta) \approx \sum_{k = 0}^{N_r} \sum_{l = 0}^{N_\theta} c^{kl} \, T_k (s_r) \, T_l (s_\theta) ,
\tag{3}
$$
normalized in each direction as in [Spectral Methods](spectral.qmd#computing-the-coefficients).
Both levels start at `level-min`. The grids of consecutive levels are nested, so raising a
level by one keeps every sample and evaluates $G$ only at the new nodes of that direction.

The function $G$ is an [[numcosmo-math|NcmSpectralPolarF]]: one call fills the values at one
radius and at the angles of the panel that have no value yet, and receives those angles
with their cosines and sines. The cosines and sines are computed once per angle of a panel
and used for every radius of it.

## The Test

The test is Eq. (2) of [Spectral Methods](spectral.qmd#adaptive-refinement) in each
direction. Let
$$
b_r^k \equiv \sum_{l = 0}^{N_\theta} \left| c^{kl} \right|, \qquad
b_\theta^l \equiv \sum_{k = 0}^{N_r} \left| c^{kl} \right|
$$
be the $\ell_1$ norms of the coefficients at a fixed radial and at a fixed angular index.
The coefficients of the grid with every other radial node are those of Eq. (3) folded in
$k$, and the same holds in $l$ for every other angle, so the $\ell_1$ changes of the
coefficients from those two coarser grids are
$$
D_r \equiv 2 \sum_{k > N_r / 2} b_r^k, \qquad
D_\theta \equiv 2 \sum_{l > N_\theta / 2} b_\theta^l .
\tag{4}
$$
Since $|T_k| \le 1$, $D_r$ bounds the largest change of the interpolant on the panel when
the radial grid is coarsened, and $D_\theta$ the same for the angular grid. The panel is
accepted when
$$
D_r + D_\theta \le \max \left( \varepsilon_\mathrm{rel} V, \; \varepsilon_F \right) ,
\tag{5}
$$
where $V$ is the largest $|F|$ on the grid of the panel and $\varepsilon_\mathrm{rel}$ is
the relative tolerance. The first term, $\varepsilon_\mathrm{rel} V$, is proportional to
the largest $|F|$ on the panel. The second,
$$
\varepsilon_F \equiv \frac{\max \left( \varepsilon_\mathrm{rel} |I|, \; \varepsilon_\mathrm{abs} \right)}{W},
\qquad
W \equiv \sum_\mathrm{panels} (r_b - r_a)^{1 + c_a + c_b} \, \mathrm{B} (1 + c_a, 1 + c_b) \, (\theta_b - \theta_a) ,
\tag{6}
$$
is the change of $F$ that, on every panel at once, changes the integral by
$\max (\varepsilon_\mathrm{rel} |I|, \varepsilon_\mathrm{abs})$: $W$ is the integral over
all the panels of the weight left out of $F$, with $\mathrm{B}$ the Beta function, and
$\varepsilon_\mathrm{abs}$ is the absolute tolerance in the units of $I$. With this term, a
panel where $F$ is negligible against the whole integral satisfies Eq. (5) on its starting
grid.

Both sides of Eq. (5) are estimates. The sum $D_r + D_\theta$ is the change between grids,
not the distance to $F$, and a feature of $F$ located between the nodes of both grids does
not change it.

## Refinement

A panel that does not satisfy Eq. (5) is refined in the direction with the larger change:
the radial one when $D_r \ge D_\theta$, the angular one otherwise.

- The level of that direction is raised by one, unless one of the two cases below holds.
- When the level of that direction is `level-cap`, the panel is bisected in that
  direction.
- When the level is one below `level-cap` and the next doubling is predicted to fail, the
  panel is bisected as well. The prediction is the one of
  [Spectral Methods](spectral.qmd#batch-expansions), applied to $b_r^k$ or $b_\theta^l$ and
  compared with the right-hand side of Eq. (5).

The two halves of a bisected panel start again at `level-min` in both directions, with the
exponents $c_a$ and $c_b$ of their own ends. A panel that needs a bisection after
`max-depth` bisections sets the error `NCM_SPECTRAL_POLAR_ERROR_MAX_DEPTH`, and the
integral returned is NaN.

## The Value of a Panel

Integrating Eq. (3) against the weight left on the panel gives
$$
I_\mathrm{panel} = h_r^{1 + c_a + c_b} \, h_\theta \sum_{k, l} c^{kl} \, M^r_k \, M^\theta_l ,
\tag{7}
$$
with the moments
$$
M^r_k \equiv \int_{-1}^{1} (1 + s)^{c_a} (1 - s)^{c_b} \, T_k (s) \, \mathrm{d}s, \qquad
M^\theta_l \equiv \int_{-1}^{1} T_l (s) \, \mathrm{d}s .
$$
The moment $M^\theta_l$ is $2 / (1 - l^2)$ for even $l$ and zero for odd $l$, the
Clenshaw--Curtis moments of [Spectral Methods](spectral.qmd#spectral-integration), and so
is $M^r_k$ when $c_a = c_b = 0$. Otherwise $M^r_k$ is computed by a Gauss--Jacobi rule of
$N_r / 2 + 2$ nodes, which is exact for the degree $N_r$ of $T_k$. The power laws are
therefore integrated exactly against the interpolant, and the error of a panel is that of
Eq. (3).

## The Estimate of the Integral

The term $\varepsilon_F$ needs $|I|$ before the integral is known. The call proceeds in
three steps.

1. Every panel given by the edges is sampled on its starting grid. The sum $I_0$ of the
   values of Eq. (7) on those grids replaces $I$ in Eq. (6).
2. Each panel is accepted or refined with that $\varepsilon_F$, starting from the samples
   of step 1.
3. The values of the accepted panels are summed. If the sum gives a smaller
   $\varepsilon_F$, the accepted panels are tested again with it, from the $D_r + D_\theta$
   and $V$ they were accepted with; those that fail are expanded again from `level-min`.
   This step repeats until no accepted panel fails.

Step 3 changes the result when a starting grid has a node at a maximum much narrower than
its panel: $I_0$ is then many times $I$, and a panel whose change is above the final
$\varepsilon_F$ can be accepted in step 2 by the larger $\varepsilon_F$ computed from
$I_0$.

## Edges for One Peak

The function [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_polar_peak_edges]] gives the edges for an
integrand with one maximum at $(r_\mathrm{p}, \theta_\mathrm{p})$ of half widths $L_r$ and
$L_\theta$, with $\omega > 1$ the property `edge-ratio` and $n \ge 1$ the property
`min-radial-panels` (default 2).

- Radial edges: $0$, $R$, $k R / n$ for $k = 1, \dots, n - 1$, and
  $r_\mathrm{p} \pm L_r \omega^\nu$, $\nu = 0, 1, \dots$, for the values inside
  $(0, R)$. After sorting, an edge closer than $L_r / 4$ to the one before is left out,
  except $R$.
- Angular edges: $\theta_\mathrm{p} \pm \pi$ and $\theta_\mathrm{p} \pm L_\theta \omega^\nu$,
  $\nu = 0, 1, \dots$, for the values farther than $L_\theta / 4$ from
  $\theta_\mathrm{p} \pm \pi$. When $L_\theta \ge \pi / 4$ the full circle is split into
  four equal panels with $\theta_\mathrm{p}$ at the center of one.

The panel that contains the maximum is $2 L_r$ by $2 L_\theta$, and the widths of the
panels increase by the factor $\omega$ with the distance to it. On a panel that does not
contain the maximum, $F$ is largest on the side nearest to it, where the Lobatto grid has
nodes. The position and the widths only place the edges: with other values the number of
evaluations of $G$ changes, and Eq. (5) is applied to every panel in the same way.

The edges $k R / n$ bound the width of the panels far from the maximum. Eq. (5) estimates
the error of a panel from the change between two grids, and a wide panel far from the
maximum can pass it with a larger error: for the shape marginal of
[Shape Marginalization by Spectral Panels](../../nc/lss/galaxy/wl_shape_marginalization_spectral.qmd)
at `reltol` $10^{-4}$, the largest error with $n = 1$ is 25 times the one with the default
$n = 2$. A larger $n$ gives more panels of lower degree, which is also cheaper for an
approximation that is evaluated many times
([Approximation on the Panels](#approximation-on-the-panels)): one evaluation costs
$(N_r + 1) (N_\theta + 1)$ multiplications.

## Approximation on the Panels

The function [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_polar_build]] expands a function $F (r, \theta)$
on the panels of the edges and keeps the coefficients $c^{kl}$ of Eq. (3) of every
accepted panel in an [[numcosmo-math|NcmSpectralPolarPanels]]. It differs from the
integral in three points.

- There is no weight: $F$ is expanded as given on every panel, and Eq. (2) is not used.
- The test is Eq. (5) with $\varepsilon_F$ given by the caller, the argument `abstol` in
  the units of $F$, instead of Eq. (6). It is the $\varepsilon_\mathrm{abs}$ of
  [Spectral Methods](spectral.qmd#adaptive-refinement). One of `reltol` and `abstol` may be
  zero.
- Each panel is tested once: the three steps of
  [The Estimate of the Integral](#the-estimate-of-the-integral) are needed only because
  Eq. (6) depends on $I$.

The grids, the doubling and the bisection are those of [Refinement](#refinement). The
panels given by the edges are the initial panels; an initial panel that was bisected holds
several panels, which cover it without overlap.

The function [[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_polar_panels_eval]] evaluates the approximation
at a point $(r, \theta)$.

1. The initial panel is found by bisection over the radial edges and over the angular edges.
   The panels of that initial panel are then searched in the order they were accepted.
2. On the panel, with $s_r$ and $s_\theta$ of the point, a Clenshaw recurrence in $s_r$
   gives $u^l \equiv \sum_k c^{kl} T_k (s_r)$ for each angular index $l$, and a Clenshaw
   recurrence in $s_\theta$ over the $u^l$ gives Eq. (3). This takes
   $(N_r + 1) (N_\theta + 1)$ multiplications.

A point on an edge belongs to the panel that starts there. A point outside the edges is
assigned to the nearest panel, whose series is extrapolated. The angle is not wrapped: the
caller gives $\theta$ inside $[\theta_0, \theta_{n_\theta}]$.

The remark below Eq. (5) applies to the approximation directly: $D_r + D_\theta$ is the
change between grids, so a maximum of $F$ that is below $\varepsilon_F$ at every node of
a panel is absent from its coefficients, and the panel is accepted without it. The edges
must therefore be placed from the known position and width of such a maximum, as
[Edges for One Peak](#edges-for-one-peak) does.

## Symbols and the Code

| symbol | in `ncm_spectral_polar.c` |
|---|---|
| $r_a, r_b, \theta_a, \theta_b$ | `ra`, `rb`, `ta`, `tb` of a panel |
| $l_r, l_\theta$; $N_r, N_\theta$ | `lx`, `ly`; `n`, `m` |
| $r^{a - c_a} (R - r)^{b - c_b}$ at the radial nodes | `wr` |
| $c^{kl}$, before the normalization | `coeffs`, row $l$, column $k$ |
| $b_r^k$, $b_\theta^l$ | `br`, `bt` |
| $D_r$, $D_\theta$, $V$ | `Dr`, `Dt`, `vs` |
| $\varepsilon_F$, $W$ | `abstol_F`, `A` of the call |
| $M^r_k$, $M^\theta_l$, times the normalization of $c^{kl}$ | the tables of `mom`, `mt` |
| $\varepsilon_F$ of a build | `abstol_F` of the call, equal to `abstol` |
| $c^{kl}$ of an accepted panel of a build | `coeffs` of `NcmSpectralPolarPanels`, row $l$, column $k$ |

The transform of a grid is two one-dimensional passes. A direction with 9 or 17 nodes is
transformed by the product with the DCT-I matrix, applied to the even and odd parts of the
lines; a direction with more nodes by an FFTW `REDFT00` plan.

## API Reference

See [[numcosmo-math|NcmSpectralPolar]] for the full class reference:
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_polar_integrate]] and
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_polar_peak_edges]], with the properties `level-min`,
`level-cap`, `max-depth`, `edge-ratio` and `min-radial-panels`. On request,
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_polar_integrate]] also returns the accepted panels, one row
per panel with $r_a$, $r_b$, $\theta_a$, $\theta_b$, $l_r$, $l_\theta$, the value of
Eq. (7) and $D_r + D_\theta$, for inspecting where the panels were refined.

See [[numcosmo-math|NcmSpectralPolarPanels]] for the approximation:
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_polar_build]] fills it, and
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_polar_panels_eval]],
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_polar_panels_find_panel]] and
[[numcosmo-math|ncm_spectral_polar_panels_peek_panel]] read it.
